notes.text: A step is bound only to an action id that authority-bindings.json lists, with that element's Surface. Keyboard shortcuts (EL-KEY-*), code-behind pointer handlers (scrims, format cards, the pitch/aspect/exclude rows, the preview frame), sliders, text inputs, timeline pointer operations (TimelineControl), window operations, DragOver/DropFile, OpenLanguageMenu and SetFastExport have no Command binding in Views/*.axaml and are left unbound. Where a bound element runs the same command (e.g. Space -> TogglePlayCommand, bound at TransportView), it was NOT substituted, because the harness checks the surface (iii) and the availability (ii) of the bound element, which would certify a different element than the scenario names; the unbound_steps entry names the same-command binding so the experimenter can decide.
A scenario with any unbound step is left out of harness-scenarios.json whole (not truncated, and not marked harness:no, which is kept for file dialogs and external processes).

The id Scale:1 appears twice: the 100% button (conds HasClip) and the Reset button (conds HasClip, ShowReset). EL-INS-SCALE-100 (UC-112) and EL-INS-SCALE-RESET (UC-107 step 2) both bind to Scale:1 @ InspectorView; the action id cannot say which element, so the harness may check the Reset button's ShowReset condition on the 100% press or not check it on the Reset press.

The schema's example action id SelectFormat:Mp4 is not in authority-bindings.json Elements; SelectFormatCommand is called only from ExportDialogView.axaml.cs OnFormatCardPressed (listed under CodeBehind). Every format-card step (EL-EX-FORMAT-*) is therefore unbound.

It uses public settable VM properties (Playhead, Playing, SelectedId, Edited, OutW, OutH, ShowExport, ShowAbout, ShowFfmpegSetup, IsExporting, ExportProgress, ExportFrame, ExportStatus, FfmpegSetupError) and DocumentState methods (SplitAt, SetVolume, SetSpeed, DeleteBoundary, MoveTrim, MoveBoundary). notes.where: start points that depend on the machine (written)
notes.text: The fresh VM sets ShowFfmpegSetup = !FfmpegLocator.Available. The scenarios' premise is that ffmpeg is available, so ShowFfmpegSetup = false is NOT forced by setup in the ordinary scenarios; on a machine without ffmpeg they fail (i). UC-191, UC-192, UC-220, UC-234 set ShowFfmpegSetup = true by setup (the overlay only; the premise behind it - ffmpeg missing, half-installed - is not reproduced; UC-234's MOVIEPAD_SCENARIO=ffmpeg is exactly this assignment). UC-192's FfmpegSetupError is set to the fixed prefix only (the exception text is unknown and is not checked). UC-194 (ffprobe absent) and UC-202 (THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt absent next to the executable) have premises that no setup op can set; they are written with no setup and depend on the harness machine and output folder.

Open (UC-140, UC-141, UC-142, UC-143, UC-194), ConfirmExport (UC-162, UC-175, UC-176) and InstallFfmpeg (UC-191, UC-192) are written with harness: no; their action ids carry no parameter, so the chosen path of Open/ConfirmExport (or null for a dialog closed without choosing, UC-143/UC-176) is not represented. UC-162 is ConfirmExport on the sample: ConfirmExport returns at clip.Path empty before PickSavePathAsync, so it opens no dialog and could be executed safely if the experimenter wants its expect (ST-SE-EXPORT) checked.

UC-052 presses Set Out while CanSetTrimOut is false (the scenario records that nothing happens, expect = in). The harness requires the action to be available (ii), so this step fails by construction; the scenario's meaning was kept.

UC-020 and UC-022 execute TogglePlay, whose StartPlayback starts a DispatcherTimer when UseExternalPlayback is false. UseExternalPlayback was not set by setup (the scenarios are about the sample's own timer); if the harness has no dispatcher loop and the timer start throws or ticks between steps, setting UseExternalPlayback = true in setup is the schema's own remedy.

Almost all TimelineView attributes (pxPerSec, contentWidth, rulerStep, scrollOffset, dragMode, hoverBoundary, cursor) live in TimelineControl or are doubles, so the zoom scenarios UC-064 / UC-065 check only TimelineSummary, RegionCount, SelectedId and ThumbnailsRefining; PxPerSec (double) is not checked.

notes.where: setup ops not checked by any predicate
notes.text: Of the 60 setup ops, 7 set a value that no predicate of their scenario checks and are there only so the start point matches the real state: Edited = true in UC-038, UC-039, UC-040, UC-044, UC-087, UC-112, and FfmpegSetupError (prefix only) in UC-192. Numbers for double targets (Playhead, the time and fps arguments of SplitAt / MoveTrim / MoveBoundary) are written as JSON reals (20.0, 30.0), ints for int targets.
scenarios.json has no goal field; goal is written equal to the title. The requirement field of scenarios.json is not part of section 3 and is not carried.

SwitchLanguage calls AppSettings.Load/Save and writes the settings file of the user running the harness. Every scenario with SwitchLanguage also has OpenLanguageMenu (unbound), so none is written; if OpenLanguageMenu becomes bindable, the harness should isolate the settings path first.
